result: In 246 glandular fever patients, 9.4% had chronic fatigue at 3 months and 7.8% met CFS criteria at 6 months; baseline anxiety, depression, somatisation, perfectionism, negative illness beliefs and all-or-nothing behaviour (strongest) predicted CFS, while perceived stress and activity limitation did not.
reason: Not an adolescent incidence study; it tests psychological predictors of post-infective CFS, which contradicts the claim that psychological factors do not predict it; incidence also bears on the Dubbo 6-month rate.

result: Blinded multi-lab Western blot, ELISA and nested PCR found no XMRV in 51 CFS cases and 53-56 US controls (one weak unconfirmed ELISA reactivity in each group).
reason: Independent blinded negative study of the same measure, in line with the refutation; Switzer 2010 not among cited studies.

result: In a new cohort, ventricular CSF lactate by 1H MRSI was higher in 17 CFS than 19 healthy controls, MDD (n=21) did not differ from either group, lactate correlated with mental fatigue only in CFS, and GABA and Glx were unchanged.
reason: Same measure and group, a second cohort (Murrough 2010) not among cited studies; MDD overlap fits the non-specificity point.

result: In 99 CFS patients and 64 controls (postal questionnaires), CFS had greater functional impairment (PROMIS HAQ 36 vs 6), and orthostatic symptom scores were associated with functional impairment.
reason: Measures self-reported orthostatic symptoms and function, not POTS prevalence; no atlas finding covers this, and the abstract results are truncated.

result: In 20 CFS vs 20 matched controls, time- and frequency-domain HRV during sleep was significantly lower (all p<0.006) and was the best predictor of poorer subjective sleep quality.
reason: Measures nocturnal HRV, which the newer neuro-nocturnal-hrv finding covers; for neuro-hrv (resting HRV) it would be extends.

result: In 20 CFS vs 20 matched controls, HRV during sleep was lower and predicted poorer subjective sleep quality; repeated awakening was reported 7 times more often.
reason: Sleep outcomes are subjective only, not polysomnography; the HRV result is handled by the neuro-hrv / nocturnal-HRV link.

result: In 12 CFS vs 8 controls, cardiac PCr/ATP correlated with muscle PCr and ADP recovery half-times (r -0.71 and -0.60); 4 of 12 had cardiac PCr/ATP showing marked impairment, and these patients had reduced maximal and initial muscle proton efflux.
reason: Same Newcastle muscle 31P-MRS proton-efflux measure, adding a link between a cardiac-energetics subgroup and impaired acid handling; Hollingsworth 2010 not among cited studies.

result: Cardiac PCr/ATP was impaired in 4 of 12 CFS patients and was associated with increased cardiac contractility (LVWI by impedance cardiography) on standing.
reason: Measures cardiac energetics and contractility index, not LV volumes or stroke volume; no finding covers cardiac PCr/ATP.

result: Six months after mononucleosis, 21 adolescents with CFS had lower peak VO2 % predicted (99.3 vs 110.7, P=.05) and peak oxygen pulse (12.4 vs 14.9, P=.03) than 21 recovered controls, with no difference in peak work capacity.
reason: Same maximal CPET peak-VO2 measure, same direction, in an independent adolescent post-infectious cohort; effect is small and borderline.

result: In the Katz post-mono adolescent cohort, CFS cases at 6 months had lower peak VO2 % predicted (99.3 vs 110.7) and peak oxygen pulse than recovered controls.
reason: Does not measure post-mono CFS incidence or persistence; the exercise result is handled by the low-peak-VO2 link.
